      "body": "\nSizes are consistent with MEMORY USAGE now that #5092 is on unstable; it made the same fix as #4981, which this PR used to include as its first commit. Independent of #4980, but #4980 fixes a crash that post notification jobs can trigger, and the docs below recommend those jobs for writes.\n\nThis adds module API, so I expect it to go through the major-decision process. The implementation is complete and tested so the discussion can be concrete; I'm happy to move the API discussion to an issue if that's preferred.\n\n#### Motivation\nModules that attribute dataset memory and Pub/Sub usage to groups of keys or channels (per prefix or namespace, e.g. for accounting or limits in multi-tenant deployments) have no efficient way to learn how sizes change.\n\nKeyspace notifications plus `MEMORY USAGE` through `ValkeyModule_Call()`:\n- run after the change, so the size before a modification or deletion is lost unless the module shadows every key;\n- cost a command call per notification;\n- fire per command, exposing a transaction's or script's intermediate states;\n- miss size changes that are never notified: hashtables rehashed or shrunk by reads, by active defrag, or by a background iteration releasing a value.\n\nFor Pub/Sub, modules can only poll `PUBSUB NUMSUB` for channels they already know about.\n\n#### `ValkeyModuleEvent_KeyMemoryDelta`\n```c\ntypedef struct ValkeyModuleKeyMemoryDelta { /* V1, VALKEYMODULE_KEYMEMORYDELTA_VERSION */\n    uint64_t version;\n    ValkeyModuleString *key; /* valid during the callback; ValkeyModule_HoldString() to keep it */\n    uint64_t old_bytes;      /* MEMORY USAGE before, 0 if the key didn't exist */\n    uint64_t new_bytes;      /* MEMORY USAGE after, 0 if the key doesn't exist */\n    int32_t dbnum, old_exists, new_exists;\n    int32_t loading_dataset; /* non-zero for a key of the dataset an async load is loading */\n} ValkeyModuleKeyMemoryDeltaV1;\n```\n- **Per-unit coalescing.** Fires once per key whose existence or size changed, when the outermost execution unit completes. A unit is a command, a whole MULTI/EXEC or script, a module timer or event callback, or the expiration or eviction of a key.\n  - Delivery is after the post notification jobs and before propagation.\n  - No-op writes produce nothing.\n  - Keys are reported in their final db (e.g. after SWAPDB), in no particular order.\n- **Sizes** are exactly `MEMORY USAGE <key>` with the default samples, and they telescope. An event's old fields match the previous event's new fields for that key, so running totals are exact. For aggregates, the per-event difference is a sampled estimate, as MEMORY USAGE is.\n- **Loading.**\n  - Every key loaded from an RDB (disk or full sync) is reported, before its `loaded` notification.\n  - Every key modified while replaying an AOF is reported. Each replayed command, or MULTI/EXEC transaction, is one execution unit, as in live execution, without refreshing the cached time.\n  - During `ReplAsyncLoad`, events describe both datasets. Keys of the dataset being loaded have `loading_dataset` set and the db number they will replace. Changes to the served dataset, which is kept if the load is aborted, have `loading_dataset` 0. In both cases the callback's selected db is the served dataset's `dbnum`.\n- **No per-key events for whole-db operations.** FLUSHDB, FLUSHALL, SWAPDB and the async-load swap are covered by the existing FlushDB, SwapDB and ReplAsyncLoad events.\n- **Callbacks must not modify the keyspace.** This is the Key event's rule. They can use `ValkeyModule_AddPostNotificationJob()`, which then runs in the same unit, and its writes are reported by further events. As for KSN and the Key event, lazy expiration is disabled during callbacks.\n\n#### `ValkeyModuleEvent_PubSubSubscriptionDelta`\n```c\ntypedef struct ValkeyModulePubSubSubscriptionDelta { /* V1, VALKEYMODULE_PUBSUBSUBSCRIPTIONDELTA_VERSION */\n    uint64_t version;\n    ValkeyModuleString *channel;               /* valid during the callback */\n    uint64_t old_subscribers, new_subscribers; /* absolute counts */\n    int32_t sharded;\n} ValkeyModulePubSubSubscriptionDeltaV1;\n```\n- **When it fires:** whenever the number of clients subscribed to a channel or shard channel changes. That covers (S)SUBSCRIBE, (S)UNSUBSCRIBE (including \"all\"), RESET, client disconnection (including async frees), and removal of the shard channels of a slot no longer served.\n- **Counts are absolute,** so a consumer can resynchronize from any event. Duplicate subscribes emit nothing.\n- **Patterns are not reported:** they don't map to one channel.\n- **Ordering:** subscribe events fire after the confirmation is queued to the client, so messages a callback publishes follow it. Callbacks must not change subscriptions.\n\n#### Design (KeyMemoryDelta)\n- **Snapshot at first touch.** The first time a key is touched in a unit, its existence and MEMORY USAGE are recorded with a copy of its name. At delivery the key is looked up again with `dbFind()`, as MEMORY USAGE does. Each batch is fully sampled before any callback runs.\n- **Single-key units allocate nothing.** The first key goes to a static snapshot whose name buffer is reused, and further keys go to a hashtable. RDB-loaded keys are reported straight from the value at hand.\n- **No value pointers are kept.** Values can be reallocated (embedding a TTL, `dbUnshareStringValue()`, defrag) or freed (DEL, lazyfree, overwrite) before the unit ends. Keeping pointers would need invalidation in all of those paths.\n- **Zero cost without subscribers.** Every data-path hook is a `static inline` wrapper that tests one global listener count before evaluating anything, including the key name.\n\n**Alternatives considered:**\n- **`signalModifiedKey()` / keyspace notifications.** These fire after the change, per command rather than per unit, and not at all for read-triggered or background resizes.\n- **A size cached in object metadata.** That adds 8 bytes per key for every user, needs exact accounting in every type's mutation paths, and diverges from the sampled MEMORY USAGE.\n- **Converting read-then-modify lookups (GETEX, HGETEX, XREADGROUP…) to `lookupKeyWrite()`.** That changes keyspace hits/misses, keymiss notifications and replica expiry; see the PFCOUNT comment in `hyperloglog.c`. Instead, `lookupKey()` checks the executing command's `CMD_WRITE` flag, as it already consults flags for `no_touch`.\n- **Leaving background resizes unreported.** The next `old_bytes` would no longer match the previous `new_bytes`, and summing consumers would drift.\n- **Extending `ValkeyModuleEvent_Key`.** It is synchronous, carries the value, and fires only on unlink/overwrite. Changing it would change its cost and semantics for existing subscribers.\n\n#### Hook inventory\n| Where | Why |\n|---|---|\n| `lookupKey()` hit | Write lookups; reads of values whose hashtables may rehash or shrink on read (scans and random sampling resume paused auto-shrink). List reads aren't tracked: since #4782 they don't change a quicklist |\n| GETEX, HGETEX, XREADGROUP, XACK, XCLAIM, XAUTOCLAIM | The only write commands that modify a key they looked up for reading; they track it after the lookup |\n| `dbAddInternal()`, `dbSetValue()`, `dbGenericDeleteWithDictIndex()` | State before add / overwrite / delete |\n| `dbReclaimExpiredFields()` | Fields are deleted before the batch's unit starts. Tracked only if a field is due, or the volatile set's RAX can collapse to its single bucket (listpacks always) |\n| `evictSingleKey()` | Track the value eviction already found, before `zmalloc_used_memory()` is read, so the snapshot isn't counted against the freed memory |\n| `defragKey()`, `defragLaterItem()`, background-iteration item return | Resuming a value's paused rehashing may shrink it, outside any command; defragmenting a hash with a RAX-backed volatile set may restructure that set's hashtable buckets |\n| `emptyData()`, `discardTempDb()`, `swapMainDbWithTempDb()` | Drop snapshots of databases emptied or replaced as a whole |\n| `dbSwapDatabases()` | Move snapshots to the other database |\n| `rdbLoadRioInternal()`, `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile()` | Report each loaded key, then whatever its `loaded` notification changed; replay each AOF command inside an execution unit and deliver after it |\n| `postExecutionUnitOperations()` | Delivery, after post notification jobs, before propagation; loops for jobs added by callbacks |\n| `beforeSleep()` | Delivers changes tracked outside any unit (defrag, background iteration, routing lookups), and doesn't sleep while some are left; only bounds the delay |\n| `hashtableNeedsShrink()` | Shrink predicate split out of `hashtableShrinkIfNeeded()`, no behavior change (gtest); also fixes the `keyCompare` comment in hashtable.h |\n| `OBJ_COMPUTE_SIZE_DEF_SAMPLES` | Moved to server.h so events use MEMORY USAGE's default |\n| `pubsubSubscribeChannel()`, `pubsubUnsubscribeChannel()`, `pubsubShardUnsubscribeAllChannelsInSlot()` | The three places a channel's subscriber count changes |\n\n#### Performance\n**No subscriber.** Each per-key hook is one load and a not-taken branch. Changed the check to follow the upstream Redis 8.0-M02 fix:

```c
if ((flags & LOOKUP_NOTOUCH) == 0 &&
    server.current_client && server.current_client->flag.no_touch &&
    server.executing_client && server.executing_client->cmd->proc != touchCommand)
    flags |= LOOKUP_NOTOUCH;
```
